SP_ACTINOCYCLUS_VERRUCOSUS_EHRENBERG_183: Actinocyclus verrucosus Ehrenberg, 1831 -- the same genus name as the diatom Actinocyclus (hemidiscaceae), but NCBI's own NameUsage.tsv carries a SEPARATE ICZN-coded taxon (id 262595, no author) under family Actinocyclidae / superfamily Eudoridoidea, the same nudibranch family we hold Hallaxa in. The Australian Faunal Directory import independently agrees -- it reintroduced this exact species (plus papillatus, laevis, japonicus) into actinocyclidae.json before NCBI was ever run, which is what NCBI's copy duplicated against. Two independent sources filing the same name under the zoological family makes this a genuine homonym to confirm, not a one-off misfiling to delete.
SP_ALICEATHRIPS_AUSTRALIENSIS: CheckListBank / NCBI import (2026-10-12/13): import artifact, not a true homonym -- the animalia entry in Thripidae (checklistbank 1279082) is the real thrips species; the plantae entry in Poaceae (checklistbank ott6021347, an OTT id) is the same thrips species misplaced into grasses by the OTT merge. The animalia genus lineage is correct; the plantae copy is a duplicate carrying the wrong family context. Kept here rather than removed because at the time it was first triaged the OTT-contamination pattern had not yet been generalised into a removal rule.
SP_ALLONEMA_GLOBIFORME_CONDRA_ELIAS_1944: NOT a genuine homonym -- known WoRMS (checklistbank-2011) contamination: the plantae copy is wrong-kingdom, confirmed by the animalia/fungi copy's own self-description or authorship. Allowlisted rather than deleted because pendingFamilyWatcher.py re-runs WoRMS's own archive every cycle as new families become ready, and the archive itself still contains the bad record -- deleting it from the tree just gets it re-added on the next reimport, with no permanent per-record exclusion mechanism to stop that. 2026-10-23 overnight pass.

SP_AMPHINEMA_SP: NCBI Taxonomy import (2026-10-12): every one an indeterminate 'Genus sp.' or 'Genus aff.' placeholder, never a named species -- so each pair is two unrelated real genera (different family in each kingdom, no family-name collision) that each happen to carry an unidentified-specimen record. Checked against NCBI's own raw NameUsage.tsv chain for a sample (Giraudia: ICN brown-alga genus 86872 vs ICZN wasp genus 216146, NCBI's own annotation literally reads 'unclassified Giraudia (in: wasps, ants & bees)' -- a genuine homonym, not a collision). The same import's 21 Aliceathrips-and-friends thrips/plant-genus collisions are not here: the plant half of each pair was one of the in-family duplicates the merge collapsed, so what was a cross-kingdom homonym became a single record and there is nothing left to allow.

SP_CHONDRACANTHUS_ANGUSTATUS_HELLER_1865: eunis (checklistbank-2122) import, 2026-10-10: Chondracanthus is both a parasitic copepod genus (animalia) and a red-algae genus (plantae, Gigartinaceae), and 'angustatus Heller, 1865' happens to name a species in each. Removed from coniocybaceae.json rather than allow-listed, the same call made on ITIS's nudibranch filed under a diatom family (see docs/dataset-inbox.md).
